title: JECT: Addressing the Context Shortcut in Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning for Chest CT
abstract: arXiv:2611.31849v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architectures learn by predicting features of masked regions from visible context. In chest computed tomography, the findings that decide a diagnosis, such as a small nodule, are often not predictable from the surrounding anatomy. A hidden finding is then best predicted toward normal anatomy, and the prediction loss stops rewarding the encoder for representing it. We call this the context shortcut. Conditioning the predictor on the radiology report repairs the prediction, but in our setup the encoder gains little over image-only pretraining: the report supplies what the encoder never had to learn. JECT therefore gives the report two roles: a condition for the predictor and, through masked section-text prediction, a target for the encoder, which must predict the report's anatomical sections from the unmasked scan. A hierarchical three-dimensional encoder that predicts at every stage keeps this clinical content

translated_title: JECT：解决胸部CT联合嵌入预测学习中的上下文捷径问题
translated_abstract: 联合嵌入预测架构通过从可见上下文预测被掩码区域的特征来进行学习。在胸部计算机断层扫描（CT）中，决定诊断的关键发现（如小结节）往往无法从周围的解剖结构中预测出来。此时，被隐藏的病灶最容易被预测为正常解剖结构，预测损失不再激励编码器去表征该病灶。我们将这种现象称为“上下文捷径”。利用放射学报告对预测器进行条件化可以修复预测问题，但在我们的设置中，编码器相对于仅使用图像的预训练几乎没有提升：因为报告直接提供了编码器原本无需学习的内容。因此，JECT赋予报告两个角色：一是作为预测器的条件，二是通过掩码分节文本预测，作为编码器的预测目标——编码器必须从未掩码的扫描图像中预测出报告的解剖学分节内容。一个在每个阶段都进行预测的分层三维编码器使这些临床内容得以保留在学习表征中。
tldr: JECT通过让放射学报告同时充当预测器的条件输入和编码器的预测目标，解决了胸部CT自监督联合嵌入预测学习中“上下文捷径”导致编码器忽略病灶的问题。
en_tdlr: JECT addresses the context shortcut in joint-embedding predictive learning for chest CT by using the radiology report both as a conditioning input for the predictor and as a masked section-text prediction target for the encoder.
